principles: Flow tools return the exact structured value and mutation to apply.
Agents select schema-backed candidates instead of inventing paths or JSON descriptors.
Legacy strings remain readable for migration but cannot be introduced by new mutations.
Reference applications are inspected and dry-run only.

contract.mutation: frontend-svelte-mutate rejects non-empty string values for binding properties with FRONTEND_BINDING_REQUIRED
contract.progress: flow-app-progress validates action ids and schema paths, reports legacy strings, and returns directly executable fixes
contract.generation: FlowValueBinding path segments generate readSegments(backendResults[actionId], segments)

covered: picker candidate carries an executable mutation
legacy string and empty action id are rejected
generated Svelte reads the selected action result path

knownUnrelatedValidationDebt: The repository-level npm run check uses the builder tsconfig against generated SvelteKit aliases and reports unresolved $lib modules.
The repository-level npm run build starts Vite from the builder root and looks for _private/svelte/index.html instead of running from the generated SvelteKit project.
conclusion: P0 closes the authoring gap: the schema, picker, mutation API, progress checker and skill now share one structured binding contract. A fresh agent can apply an exact tool-produced mutation without inventing a binding representation.
